title: KDUA-Mobile: Ukrainian mobile keystroke dynamics with motion sensors, version 1.0

creators.name: Yevtushenko, Serhii V.
creators.affiliation: National University "Odesa Law Academy", Department of Cybersecurity, Odesa, Ukraine

description:
498 typing sessions from 71 people on 56 Android phones, recorded with a keyboard written for the study: every key press and release, the touch that caused it, and the motion of the phone at a requested 200 Hz while it was being typed on. Ukrainian text on the ЙЦУКЕН layout, collected between 16 September and 26 October 2026.

What is in it. 97 974 key events (48 987 press and release pairs) with per-key touch geometry, 16 608 404 samples of accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer and rotation vector, 82 participant records over 71 people and 56 devices of 46 distinct models, Android 9 to 16. Three tasks: a 16-character fixed phrase, an 89-character Ukrainian pangram typed under three conditions, and free text.

Why it is different. Most keystroke corpora record one person per device, which makes person and hardware inseparable: a classifier that tells two records apart may be telling two handsets apart, and nothing in the data can show which. This corpus breaks that confounding from both sides. 14 devices carry two or more people, giving 63 pairs of different people on identical hardware, and 11 people appear on two devices, so a template can be tested where it was not enrolled.

The condition was measured, not assumed. Each participant typed the same sentence sitting, standing, and with the phone flat on a surface. The phone's own gyroscope recorded whether it really was flat: of 90 sessions instructed that way, 74 are measurable and only 38 actually were. The instruction and the observation are separate columns, and the dataset documents which to filter on. The order of the three conditions is counterbalanced by a 3×3 Latin square assigned deterministically from the participant identifier.

Published with it: a data dictionary for every column, a quality guide, an itemised list of known defects with session identifiers, the keyboard layout key by key, the stimuli with hashes, the collection protocol, the consent text in translation, a privacy analysis with the residual leak measured rather than asserted, a fixed verification protocol, and a baseline result of 22.2 % equal error rate with the code that produces it.

Limits. 71 students of one Ukrainian university, 75 of 82 records under 20 years of age, one language, one layout. Nothing here supports a claim about a population.

Files. kdua-mobile-1.0.zip is the complete package; unpacking it and running python code/verify.py --dataset . checks both the byte checksums and the content fingerprint. sample.zip is three sessions to look at first. The content fingerprint of this version is 00330347a3e47af885486916fd89306f73a7c5baf5124d672075726785babcf8.

notes: Do not attempt to re-identify participants, and do not combine this dataset with any list of the cohort it came from. The licence permits reuse of the data; it does not make that acceptable. See docs/privacy.md in the package.
